miniProject.title: Fully sharded training with resharding evidence
miniProject.brief: Shard the data-parallel trainer in `parallel/` from full replication to full sharding with checkpoints that survive changed layouts. This turns the memory ledger into per-rank ownership and gives the capstone its recovery story.
steps: Ledger replicated state by dtype against measured tensors after the first optimizer update; pass the TensorTonic ZeRO accounting cases and extend the CS336 sharded-optimizer tests with disjoint-data reduction and memory-saving checks.

Build a tiny gather-compute-release and reduce-scatter trainer that matches the oracle over several updates; pass the CS336 FSDP tests and log where each full weight and reduced shard lives on every rank.

Compare reshard-after-forward policies and prefetch depths on identical work with event timelines, keeping oracle equivalence; report live bytes and exposed stalls, with device traces only on two or more GPUs.

Inventory wrap groups against the largest live group and simulate four-rank hybrid ownership with both gradient reductions; construct on the meta device and configure FSDP2 on a CPU mesh, checking shard and buffer materialization, dtypes, same-policy updates and global clipping against the oracle.

Derive peak live memory and dtype-aware send volume, separating the ideal estimate from the live-state ledger and CPU simulation from device profiles; keep recompute gradient-equivalent with event counts and ledger a selective offload tier.

Round-trip model and optimizer checkpoints at one world size with next-update equivalence and ownership inspection; restore onto a smaller world size, compare against the full format, and prove the next fixed-global-batch update.
Seed gradient-scaling, clipping and replication faults plus one gather-peak budget break; show each fails its targeted check and diagnose one correctness and one memory failure from rank evidence.
deliverables: Sharded trainer with ZeRO ledgers, lifecycle logs and wrap-group inventory.
Same-size and changed-layout checkpoint restores with next-update proofs.
Peak and volume derivations, offload ledger and the negative-test evidence.

checks.name: TensorTonic: Account for ZeRO Memory by Stage
checks.note: Pass the public stage cases; follow its pooled-byte ceilings and state the rule.

checks.name: CS336 Assignment 2 sharded optimizer tests
checks.note: Pass the two-process CPU comparison including tied weights.

checks.name: CS336 Assignment 2 FSDP tests
checks.note: Pass correctness and gradient-sync on two CPU ranks before trainlab extensions.

rubric.pass: Ledgers reconcile with measured tensors and the accounting cases pass with the allocation rule stated.
rubric.strong: Disjoint-data reduction and memory savings are checked beyond the public tests.

rubric.pass: Gather and reduce-scatter runs match the oracle and logs place every weight and shard.
rubric.strong: Reshard and prefetch timelines explain one case where deeper prefetch is worse.

rubric.pass: Same-size and changed-layout restores prove next-update equivalence with ownership intact.
rubric.strong: The full-format comparison and the direct restore agree, and metadata limits are stated.

rubric.pass: Each seeded fault fails its targeted check with rank evidence kept.
rubric.strong: The gather-peak break is budgeted in advance and the diagnosis names the live window.

miniProject.feedsInto: Sharded steps, ownership ledgers and reshardable checkpoints feed model parallelism, planning, recovery and the capstone contribution.
